reason: The cited evidence supports the general idea that re-melting aids dissolution (E2) and that preheating reduces cracking (E3), but no passage provides specific evidence for the key premises that a secondary scan reduces segregation or residual stress in AlCrFeNiSi, or that real-time feedback control is effective for this purpose. The process window premise is only loosely supported by a parameter study on a different material (E1).
premises: A secondary laser re-melting pass increases diffusion and re-mixing at the liquid–solid interface, mitigating compositional segregation.
A secondary laser re-melting pass lowers thermal gradients, reducing residual stress buildup.
Real-time monitoring and feedback control can precisely control laser power and scan speed to prevent over-melting during the re-melting pass.
The proposed LPBF parameters (VED ~50–80 J/mm³, layer thickness 20–40 µm, preheating ~500°C) are viable for processing AlCrFeNiSi.
